spinney.model.description: Model card a new session starts on. The value is a card **id** from `spinney.modelCards` (a GUID, or the built-in `deepseek-flash`) — not a model name, so renaming a card never invalidates a stored session. Cards bind a user-visible name to the wire model name on a provider from `spinney.providers`; edit both in the **Model Cards** page, which the gear button beside the chat's model dropdown opens. A profile with no cards falls back to the vendored `deepseek-flash` card (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1M-token context, accepts image input).
spinney.providers.name.description: What to call this endpoint — the title of its node in the **Model Cards** page, and the name in the API-key prompt.
spinney.providers.baseUrl.description: Where the API root sits, e.g. `https://api.deepseek.com`; requests go to `POST <baseUrl>/chat/completions`. A URL containing spaces is rejected.
spinney.providers.concurrency.descriptio: How many requests may be in flight against this endpoint at once. 0 means unlimited; a card on it can cap itself further, and a request that has to wait shows a queue status.
spinney.modelCards.markdownDescription:
One selectable model per card, as structured data: a user-visible name bound to the wire model name on one provider. Edit them in [settings.json](command:workbench.action.openSettingsJson?%7B%22revealSetting%22%3A%7B%22key%22%3A%22spinney.modelCards%22%2C%22edit%22%3Atrue%7D%7D) — or in the **Model Cards** page, which opens from the gear button beside the chat's model dropdown and shows the request a card would send.

```json
"spinney.modelCards": {
  "b1e2d3f4": {
    "name": "DeepSeek Flash",
    "providerId": "deepseek",
    "oaiModel": "deepseek-flash",
    "contextWindow": 1048576,
    "vision": { "enabled": true, "transport": "deepseek" },
    "efforts": ["none", "low", "medium", "high"],
    "defaultEffort": "medium",
    "concurrency": 0
  }
}
```

A card owns its context window, its vision settings, its thinking levels and its own concurrency cap; `spinney.model` holds the id of the card a new session starts on. A profile with no cards falls back to the vendored `deepseek-flash` card. Rows that cannot be parsed are ignored and listed in the **Spinney** output channel.
spinney.modelCards.name.description: What the user calls this model — the label in the chat's model dropdown. Two cards cannot share a name (case-insensitive).
spinney.modelCards.providerId.descriptio: The id of the provider this card talks to (a key of `spinney.providers`).
spinney.modelCards.oaiModel.description: The wire model name sent as `body.model`, e.g. `deepseek-flash`. Renaming `name` does not change it.
spinney.modelCards.contextWindow.descrip: The card's context window in tokens — the budget the usage indicator divides by, not the API's max_tokens output cap.
spinney.modelCards.concurrency.descripti: How many requests this card may have in flight at once. 0 means unlimited; a card never exceeds its provider's cap.
spinney.modelCards.vision.enabled.descri: Whether this card accepts image input (attach/paste in the chat, read_image). Off means images are never sent to it.
spinney.modelCards.vision.transport.desc: How an image reaches the provider, named after the vendor dialect: 'deepseek' uploads it to `POST /files` and references the returned id (DeepSeek's own extension — the image never enters the request body), 'openai' puts a `data:` URL in an `image_url` part (the OpenAI-compatible shape).
spinney.modelCards.efforts.description: The thinking levels this card offers, in the order the chat's effort dropdown shows them. The names are free-form (the level `none` sends no `reasoning_effort` at all). One card's levels do not apply to another.
spinney.modelCards.defaultEffort.descrip: The level a new session starts on. Must be one of this card's own `efforts`.
spinney.commandTimeout.description: Maximum time (seconds) a command may run before being killed. Default 600 (10 minutes); used as the default for exec_command when the tool call does not pass its own timeout.
spinney.replyLanguage.description: Language the agent replies in. 'auto' follows the VS Code display language; the rest are the languages VS Code ships display translations for, ordered by use, each labelled with the exact name written into the system prompt. Another language name or tag can still be typed into settings.json. The chosen language is written into the system prompt, so changing it in an open conversation means the next request may miss the prompt cache and reprocess the full context — like a model or thinking-effort change.
spinney.foldToolCalls.description: Collapse tool-call cards by default in the chat tree; expand them by clicking the header. The call that is running right now stays expanded.
spinney.foldThinking.description: Collapse the reasoning/thinking block by default in the chat tree; expand it by clicking its header. The block that is streaming right now stays expanded.
spinney.promptSections.markdownDescripti:
Pre-written instruction texts offered by the button at the left of the composer, keyed by the name shown in its menu. Clicking a name inserts its text into the message box: it becomes part of your own turn, editable before you send it, and nothing is sent by the click itself. Edit them in [settings.json](command:workbench.action.openSettingsJson?%7B%22revealSetting%22%3A%7B%22key%22%3A%22spinney.promptSections%22%2C%22edit%22%3Atrue%7D%7D).

```json
"spinney.promptSections": {
  "Plan": "This is a planning task: …",
  "Implement Parallel": "Start implementing the topic we discussed. …"
}
```

A name that matches a snippet the extension ships replaces that snippet's text; any other name adds a row of its own, and the shipped snippets always stay available. A row with an empty name or empty text is ignored.
spinney.maxConcurrentSubagents.descripti: How many level-1 sub-agents the main agent may run concurrently (a slot pool; extra tasks queue).
spinney.maxLevel2Subagents.description: How many sub-sub-agents each sub-agent may start. Depth is hard-capped at 2 (no sub-sub-sub-agent).
spinney.saveSubAgentTranscripts.descript: Write each finished sub-agent's full conversation to disk as JSONL (one API message per line, meta + tool-call stats on line 1) and hand its path back to the caller.
spinney.saveSessionTranscripts.descripti: Write each finished main-agent turn to disk as JSONL (same format as sub-agent transcripts) so search_transcripts can recall earlier conversations. Session history otherwise lives only in the extension's stored state.
spinney.subAgentTranscriptDir.descriptio: Folder for transcript dumps (main-agent turns + sub-agent runs), relative to the harness root (the workspace folder, or the harness scratch folder when no folder is open); a per-session subfolder is created inside. Leave empty to use the extension's global storage.
spinney.dataDir.description: Where session data (the sessions themselves) is kept. Leave empty to use a fixed folder under the extension global storage — deliberately not named after the extension id, so renaming or reinstalling the extension never moves your history. Set it to a folder you back up (or sync) to keep that history outside this machine profile; it takes effect on the next window reload.
spinney.autoSessionTitles.description: Name sessions automatically: after the first turn, and again once the conversation has grown (at most every 2 minutes). Titles are generated by the model, falling back to the first message when the request fails. Renaming a session manually locks its title. Sessions created before this feature are named once on activation.
spinney.maxInlineToolOutput.description: Maximum size (bytes) of a search_files / list_dir / search_transcripts result returned inline. Larger results are written to a temp file and only its path plus a short preview are returned. Set 0 to always inline.
spinney.httpApi.enabled.description: Expose a local HTTP control plane on 127.0.0.1 (bearer-token gated) so an external controller such as tools/hyper-vscode can read state, wait for the agent to go idle, navigate to a node, and continue from it. Off by default; /continue lets the caller make the agent run an instruction, so treat it as a local-trust boundary.
spinney.httpApi.port.description: Port for the HTTP control plane. 0 picks a free port; the chosen port and token are written to <globalStorage>/http/<instanceId>.json for the supervisor to discover.
spinney.providers.balance.description: How this endpoint's remaining credit is read. `none` shows no wallet line, `deepseek` reads `GET /user/balance`, `openrouter` reads `GET /credits` (remaining = total credits minus usage), `moonshot` reads `GET /users/me/balance`. The readout is never retried. A row that omits this field uses the dialect known for its host (`api.deepseek.com` → `deepseek`, anything else → `none`).

spinney.diagnostics.log.description: Write a diagnostics log for this window (one file per window, in the session data folder; older ones are removed, and a file rotates at 2 MiB). It holds timings, counters and paths — never your conversation and never an API key. Use Spinney: Open Diagnostics Log to find it.
